While these 19 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 applications were not evaluated as part of this study, they were deemed worthy of mention due to their synergistic potential. 6 Interactive OTEC Location Model for the GOA One of the deliverables in Objective 3 of this study is a simplified model whereby the user may be able to quickly assess the net hypothetical OTEC power production possibility in the GOA based on a limited number of inputs, including location and technical requirements. To meet this objective, the authors developed an interactive map based on the numerical OTEC model that was developed and used as part of the Objective 2 effort of the overall study, which focused on OTEC modeling through a more complex set of inputs and outputs. In contrast, the interactive map produced as the final deliverable and presented here is a simplified and user-friendly interactive tool. The interactive map is designed with an interface where the user can make the following inputs: • Select a location from the visual atlas represented by 60 locations in the Gulf • Specify the cold-water intake depth provided as a choice of 100-m steps (not to exceed the maximum water depth at the location) • Select the cold-water pipe diameter from the provided choices of 0.5, 1.6, and 3.25 m These inputs then provide outputs as described in the following. First, the location-relevant attributes in terms of the OTEC-relevant resources are displayed. Selecting the location shows its coordinates, water depth, and the monthly average water column temperatures at several depths. The monthly average temperature is derived from measured temperature at or near the location as measured by NOAA. Assumptions were made regarding average monthly temperature for locations that did not have measured water column temperature data. Objective 2 report describes in detail how missing data was handled. Next, the output for the process is shown, including output power, and process variables (e.g., fluid flow rates, working fluid temperature and pressure, etc.) and equipment information (e.g., water intake pipe sizes, number of condensers and evaporators, heat exchanger surface area, heat exchanger heat transfer coefficient, etc.). 20 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 Finally, the LCOE calculator shows the real LCOE calculated as a function of the total equipment cost, as estimated by the authors (and documented in the Objective 2 report), assumed operation and maintenance cost, and other costs and factors, including financing interest, system life, inflation, and tax rate. Detailed approach of the factors comprising capital and operation and maintenance costs as well as real LCOE are shown in Appendices 3 and 4 of the Objective 2 report.
